definition.statistic: ND[s] = sum_{loads l not ADN} sum_t pd_l[s,t] * baseMVA * dt - sum_{generators g, gen_type in definitions.GEN_CURTAILLABLE_TYPES} sum_t pg_g[s,t] * baseMVA * dt, in MWh, dt = 24 h / num_instants; per network block (network, year, day); ADN loads = the TSO loads production zeroes after the checksum point (network.adn_load_exists / get_adn_load_idx for every DSO node); evaluation: float(np.sum(A[s])) * baseMVA * dt per array, accumulated in Python floats, loads by index then generators by index
definition.tie_rule: perm = sorted(range(n), key=lambda s: (ND[s], s)): ascending ND, exact ties -> lower original index first; new index k takes original index perm[k]; new_A = old_A[perm, :] for every operation array of the block (market arrays never permuted)
definition.array_sha: sha256 over b"<f8" + repr(shape).encode("ascii") + np.ascontiguousarray(A, dtype="<f8").tobytes() (the array as float64, C order)

definition.market: Abar[year][day][t] = sum_{s_m} pi_m[year][s_m] * A[year][day][s_m, t], A in {cost_energy_p (EUR/MWh), cost_flex (EUR/MWh)}, pi_m = planning.prob_market_scenarios[year] (production _read_market_data_from_file: [1/NumMarketScenarios] * NumMarketScenarios)
definition.operation: Abar[net][year][day][device][t] = sum_{s_o} pi_o[s_o] * A[s_o, t], A in {load.pd, load.qd, load.flexibility.active_power.upward, .downward, load.flexibility.reactive_power.upward, .downward, generator.pg, generator.qg} (p.u. on the network baseMVA, as stored), pi_o = network.prob_operation_scenarios (production _read_network_data: [1/num_oper_scenarios] * n)
definition.joint_equivalence: equal to the joint mean over the 9 (s_m, s_o) pairs with weight pi_m * pi_o (production _scenario_probability) because each array depends on one dimension only and the other dimension's weights sum to 1; checked numerically
definition.evaluation: numpy float64, np.sum(w[:, None] * A, axis=0), w the production probability vector
definition.capture_point: arrays as stored at the entry of shared_resources_planning._compute_scenario_metadata (the production scenario-checksum point: TSO and DSOs read, ADN loads not yet zeroed, shared ESS not yet added); the post-read arrays are compared separately
definition.what_it_is_not: no re-derivation of power factor / Q-P ratio, no capacity clipping, no abs() of flexibility bounds (production applies abs() at model build), no re-sampling

ev_means.explanation: the mean is AA.compute_means: np.sum(w[:, None] * A, axis=0) with w = [1/3] * 3. The products w[s] * A[s, t] are the same multiset after the permutation; np.sum along axis 0 adds the rows in index order ((r0 + r1) + r2), so a permutation changes only the ORDER of two floating additions, which can move the rounded result by a few ulp. Verified two ways: (i) recomputing the BASE mean with its rows taken in the permuted order reproduces the dependence mean bit for bit; (ii) an order-independent, exactly-rounded mean (math.fsum of the products per hour) is bitwise identical for the base and the dependence arrays. Size: two orders of a 3-term recursive sum differ by at most ~2 ulp of sum_s |w_s A[s, t]| (the textbook bound, 2 * gamma_2 * sum |x|); the difference in ulp of the RESULT is larger only where the terms have mixed signs and cancel (mean near zero)
